title: How Canadian Survivor contestant Daniel Kilby lost most of his belongings to auction after filming the show
summary: Canadian Survivor contestant Daniel Kilby lost many of his personal belongings earlier this year, including a painting of a "cheetah dressed as a general," his PlayStation 5 and many household…

image.caption: Daniel Kilby, seen at left in a screenshot from his stint on Survivor, returned to Canada to find all of his stuff was being put up for auction because he missed a few of his payments for a storage locker he'd been using. (Robert Voets/CBS)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

Canadian Survivor contestant Daniel Kilby lost many of his personal belongings earlier this year, including a painting of a "cheetah dressed as a general," his PlayStation 5 and many household appliances, after missed payments on a storage locker while he was on the show led to his belongings being put up for auction.
Kilby says a 'dumb mistake' led to about $2,000 worth of stuff in a locker going to the highest bidder

Canadian Survivor contestant Daniel Kilby lost many of his personal belongings earlier this year, including a painting of a "cheetah dressed as a general," his PlayStation 5 and many household appliances, after missed payments on a storage locker while he was on the show led to them being put up for auction.
"That's where it's been annoying … I'm like, 'Oh, I want to make a sparkling water. JK, you can't,'" said the 30-year-old game designer who now lives in Halifax.

Kilby, who'd been living in London, Ont., was renting at the time, and his lease was coming up. He didn't want to pay rent while filming the 51st season of the hit reality competition, so he stored most of his belongings in a storage locker for what he says was around $100 a month and moved in with his girlfriend in Florida.
There, he could begin his Survivor training, including learning to swim and practicing fire-making.
But on his flight to Florida in February, he says he lost his wallet. So he had to get a new debit card and update his payments. The problem? There was one payment he forgot to update.

He says he realized in mid-April — the weekend before he left to film in Fiji — that he hadn't updated his payment info with the StorageMart in London. He says he tried to call the location but couldn't update his details with the person he spoke to, and he ultimately decided to leave it until after the show was filmed.
Kilby stands next to one of his prized possessions, his 'cheetah dressed as a general' painting. (Submitted by Daniel Kilby)
At the time, he says he was more focused on living his dream and getting a shot at a million dollars on Survivor.
"I also, like, low-key did not expect them to actually auction my stuff. I thought this was like a dumb mistake that I'd have to pay when I got back," said Kilby.
Arriving home
Kilby placed 11th on the season and was voted out on the eighth episode, which aired on Nov. 11. So no million-dollar prize. Instead, he returned in June to find a very different financial matter.
The first email he read upon returning to Canada was that his storage locker — and all his stuff — was going up for auction.

While he'd been away, StorageMart had tried to contact him to update his payment information and inform him he had missed at least three payments. But since he was stuck on an island at the time with no connection to the outside world, they were unable to reach him.
"My phone is blown up. I have like a hundred emails from them being like, 'Hey, you haven't paid,'" said Kilby.

blocks.text: Kilby reached out to the storage unit company, hoping he could get his stuff back. He says he was told he would need to cough up $2,000 and retrieve his stuff immediately to do so. It was a lot of money, plus he'd need to rent a vehicle that could hold it all.
"Plus, I'm like, a lot of my stuff sucked," said Kilby, who estimates it was probably worth about $2,000 altogether.
CBC reached out to StorageMart for information on its policies around late payments and when a unit goes up for auction but didn't receive a response before publication.

StorageMart's website says there is no grace period for late payments, and that late fees will apply if payments are late, with the specifics dictated on a customer's lease. StorageMart also has an online payment portal for customers, as well as a helpline it says is operated 24/7.
Kilby came in 11th on the latest season of Survivor, which is still airing. (Robert Voets/CBS)
So he had another idea. Now that his stuff was up for auction, he could just bid on it and hope no one else was too interested.

With his bid sitting around $400, he was feeling good that he would be reunited with his belongings. But at the last second, someone with the username "Prince C" made a bid and won the auction for $441.
"It's brutal; it's sad," said Kilby. "I thought we were just winning it, so I felt kind of dumb there. But I also felt kind of relieved because I'm like, 'OK, I don't have to go pick it up.'"
'It's a funny story'
Kilby said the possessions in the locker ranged from IKEA furniture to his collection of Pokemon cards.

He tried scouring Facebook Marketplace in London after the locker sold, hoping he would see some of his stuff pop up. He even posted on Reddit, hoping someone could point him to the buyer. There are some personal belongings he wishes he could get back.

"There's, like, some sentimental thing. So I had this, like, weird painting of a cheetah dressed as a general. I thought that was really cool," said Kilby. "My mom knit a bear that's in there. That sucks."
Plus there are all the household appliances such as a SodaStream and a blender that he's needed to replace.
The rest of the stuff? He's OK to live without. Since filming the show, Kilby and his girlfriend moved to Halifax, and he says many of the items in that locker wouldn't have made the trip.
"It's a funny story, and I'm somebody who lives my life trying to do things in a way that you get a funny story at the end," said Kilby.
"It's like, hey, the passion for Survivor made me just completely [lose my stuff]."
